records.region: Northeastern Greenland, inland ice and exposed-rock belt northwest of Hudson Land, continuing through the Waltershausen Gletscher setting to its inner-fjord terminus.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The national original accounts for the complete inland-ice, rock/nunatak-margin, glacier-corridor and historical ice-front/fjord sequence. It does not establish a named natural river or representative river identity across the modeled line. The glacier and receiving-fjord labels cannot name the selected river group.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected path begins northward on inland ice, runs south into the rock/nunatak belt, bends west and southwest through its ice-margin setting, turns south/east into the lower glacier corridor and proceeds southeast to the historical glacier-front/inner-fjord setting. The source labels Waltershausen Gletscher, Hudson Land and Kejser Franz Joseph Fjord supply feature-type-specific context only.
records.completion_scope: All 68 selected parts, every intermediate join, the northern opening, rock/ice transitions, lower glacier corridor and actual displayed ending were visually compared against the permitted original at ordinary corridor scale. No material geographic interval remains unseen. Missing river identity is a naming and feature-type limitation, not a remaining map-coverage gap.

component_scope_limits: Waltershausen Gletscher is the mapped glacier context, not a river-name candidate.

The supplied connected model and sea-terminal class do not independently establish a natural river or an ordinary river mouth.
A null candidate means no name was established in this bounded pass; it does not assert that no local or official name exists.

records.region: East Greenland, Mont Forel region to the eastern inner Sermilik ice/rock coastal margin.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The original national map accounts for the selected inland-ice, mixed exposed-rock/ice and inner coastal-margin sequence but establishes no representative named natural river. Mountain, glacier and fjord labels cannot name the modeled whole object.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected path opens on inland ice, proceeds east and southeast, makes a long southward bend across the mixed ice/exposed-rock belt, turns southwest and west through successive rock-margin passages, and finishes in a short westward terminal continuation by the inner Sermilik coastal margin. Both selected fragments belong to the mainstem; there are no supplied tributary fragments.
records.completion_scope: The entire selection, including all internal joins, the stage-3 to stage-2 join and actual model endpoint, was visually compared against a continuously covering retained original. No meaningful unseen geographic interval remains. No requirement for exact banks, present-day ice position or subglacial hydraulics is imposed to establish this bounded terrain correspondence.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
